cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 50th District (previously the 52nd) since 2013. Environmental lawyer and former EPA economist. San Diego's first City Council president, with two terms on the council from 2000 to 2008. Chaired the Port of San Diego Commission in 2011.

controversies.text: Federal records show $7,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $540 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26.
Missed 10 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.5%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 2, 2025-06-03 to 2025-06-03.

In August 2006 a city-commissioned audit report found Peters and eight other current and former San Diego officials negligent in ensuring the city's financial disclosures to investors were accurate. Negligence is the lowest of three levels of potential securities fraud. The report covered the city's pension and sewer finances.
In 2007 Peters was criticized for using more than 1 million gallons of water at his home and an adjacent landscaped parcel during a drought.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements include the Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and YIMBY Action.

His campaign lists endorsements from LiUNA, the California Labor Federation (AFL-CIO), the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Giffords PAC, Moms Demand Action, the Human Rights Campaign PAC, the DCCC, the New Democrat Coalition and the San Diego County Democratic Party.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Peters on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, H-1B visas, police pay and pensions, or school vouchers and teacher pay. His campaign site is partly cut off, so some priorities may be missing. His birthplace and upbringing come from Wikipedia and Ballotpedia, not a primary record. We did not find a source for how long he has lived in California beyond his campaign's own statement of more than 30 years.

top: VP BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT · Scotts Valley, CA
money.note: Individuals gave $4,092; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 50th Congressional District in 2026. Broadcast journalist for about fifty years, including twenty years as News Director of KUSI-TV in San Diego. Covered California politics from Los Angeles starting in 1982. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Republican Party of California (listed on Ballotpedia). His campaign site says the endorsement was unanimous.
Also listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed by Reform California, plus several voter-guide groups, including Conservative California and Liberty For All.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he moved to California. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, gun policy, abortion, school choice, policing, or refusing donor money. We found no documented stance on data centers or on specific development projects. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond those listed. We could not open his campaign news releases; only their headlines were visible.

score.why: Raised $4,092, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: About fifty years in broadcast journalism, including twenty years as KUSI-TV News Director in San Diego (a newsroom management role) and a decade-plus covering California politics from Los Angeles. He has held no elected or governing office.
qual.why: He has newsroom management experience and long exposure to politics as a reporter, but no legislative, executive, legal or budget role, and this is his first run for office, so he falls in the low band.
